title: PDO changes showed no clear time-order asymmetry at four lags in 1950-2025
abstract: We tested time-order asymmetry in NOAA NCEI ERSSTv5 PDO changes at lags of 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. We used 912 months in 1950-2025 and 1,999 rank and Fourier adjusted surrogates for each test series. The main normalized third moments were 0.124754, -0.001558, -0.018942 and 0.062780. The smallest two-sided rank p-value was 0.1195, or 0.478 after a four-lag adjustment. Removal of monthly means and a linear trend did not change this conclusion. The 1950-1987 one-month signal had raw p of 0.003 and adjusted p of 0.012 within that era, but p of 0.060 across all 20 comparisons. It was absent in 1988-2025. We did not test the era difference itself. These results give no clear full-record asymmetry under the tested surrogate reference. They do not prove symmetric physical dynamics or explain the recent negative PDO run. Stationarity, one revised surface index, approximate surrogate sampling and an unmeasured power limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and reproduction steps are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: PDO change statistics and surrogate reference ranges at four fixed lags. Sensitivity tests show an early one-month signal that is absent in the later era.
